title: Edge-aware capacity shield for SLO-driven multi-region request routing
creator: Maya Lindstrom
description: Implement an "edge-aware capacity shield" request routing policy that combines latency-based steering, geo-pinning preferences, and capacity headroom signals to meet p95/p99 SLOs while minimizing cross-region egress and customer-facing errors.
background: We currently use a hybrid latency/capacity steering layer but have recurring incidents where sudden localized saturation in a POP causes noisy neighbor tail latency spikes and downstream cascading retries. Some cross-region fallbacks increase egress costs and break locality-sensitive workloads. PMs and SREs asked for a policy that: 1) prioritizes SLOs (p95/p99 latency and error-rate), 2) respects geo-pinning and data locality preferences, and 3) sheds or degrades gracefully when capacity headroom is low.
design_notes: Core components: 1) Edge capacity signal: per-POP rolling headroom metric (free_gpus_percent and batch_queue_depth) aggregated to a single headroom score in [0,1]. 2) Latency penalty: compute realtime p95 delta relative to SLO; convert to penalty in [0,1]. 3) Geo-weighting: start from customer pin weight (default 0.9) and allow temporary relaxation down to min_pin=0.4 when headroom<0.15. 4) Circuit-breaker tie-in: open circuit for routing to a POP when combined error_rate>5% AND p95>SLO*1.5 for 30s. 5) Shedding strategy: soft-degrade path (route to small-quantized model variant or degrade cacheable features) when headroom<0.08; hard-shed (429) only if headroom<0.03 and all fallback regions report headroom<0.05. 6) Backoff hysteresis: use a 60s window to avoid flip-flopping and apply exponential cool-off on reattach.
tradeoffs:
- Aggressive geo relaxation reduces data locality and may increase egress; mitigated by weighted relaxation and preference for nearest fallback.
- Soft-degrades (smaller model) risk lowered output quality; we limit to non-SLA customers first and surface quality regression metrics.
- Circuit-breaker thresholds tuned conservatively to avoid tripping on transient blips; may allow short SLO misses before shedding to prefer availability.
rollout_plan:
1) Feature-flagged deployment to routing staging with synthetic traffic tests (latency profiles, saturation tests). 2) Canary rollout to 5% of production traffic (non-SLA orgs) with RouteHealth and cost telemetry. 3) Gradual ramp to 50% then 100% after 2 stable weeks. 4) Emergency kill switch and revert plan in Console.
- Milestones: staging tests (2026-02-12), canary start (2026-02-22), canary evaluation (2026-03-01).
metrics_and_alerting: New metrics: pop_headroom_score, pop_p95_delta_ratio, pop_error_rate_5m, routing_reject_rate, soft_degrade_rate, geo_relax_events. Alerts: page when pop_headroom_score<0.03 for >3m OR routing_reject_rate>0.5% sustained 5m. SLO dashboard additions: p95 and p99 per-region and for routed-fallback paths, cost per-request delta for cross-region egress.
acceptance_criteria: Routing policy deployed behind feature flag and exercised in staging with synthetic saturations
Canary (5%) shows no increase in global p99 beyond 10% relative to baseline after 24h under mixed workloads
Soft-degrade triggers for simulated headroom<0.08 and routes to quantized variant without circuit-breaker false positives
Circuit-breaker trips and recovers per spec in chaos tests (error_rate>5% AND p95>SLO*1.5 for 30s)
New dashboards show headroom and routing outcomes; on-call runbook updated
Documentation for operators and PMs (Console feature, opt-outs, and data locality implications) published

notes: Initial experiments show 18-24% reduction in cross-region egress for geo-relaxed traffic while improving p95 tail by ~12% under noisy neighbor tests. Quality regressions from soft-degrade are visible only on long-form generation and are gated by customer tier. Post-rollout A/B will measure user-facing regressions.
